newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Joulwan visits Romania to discuss PFP, Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: Joulwan visits Romania to discuss PFP, Bosnia.

text.p: U.S. Army General George Joulwan, Supreme Allied Commander of NATO Forces in Europe, started a two-day visit to Romania on Wednesday to discuss military cooperation with the former communist country.

"I'm here to thank Romania for leadership and participation in the Partnership for Peace (PFP) programme," Joulwan said before starting talks with Romanian army chief-of-staff General Dumitru Cioflina.

In January 1994 Romania was the first ex-Soviet bloc member to join the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation's PFP scheme of forging closer military ties with former Cold War foes. It has been an enthusiastic participant in PFP programmes.
Joulwan is expected to meet Romania's President Ion Iliescu and Defence Minister Gheorghe Tinca to discuss cooperation within the NATO-led IFOR peacekeeping effort in Bosnia.
The military has spearheaded Romania's diplomatic efforts to boost the Balkan country's chances of being considered among the first candidates for future membership of the Western defence alliance.
"I came to thank Romanian officials and the Romanian people for their commitment to the Implementation Force (IFOR) in Bosnia," Joulwan said.
